subject: Implementation transition: Artera SDK instrumentation & failure-safety

From: Jared Simons <jared@artera.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Artera → Redwood: kickoff + SDK + migration window

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. I’m Jared (platform lead at Artera). We’re ready to start the implementation phase for the initial integration (embedding + chat fallback). High-level asks from our side: sample SDK usage (Node + Python), recommended retry/timeouts for medium-latency workflows, guidance for endpoint cutover (staging → production), and a short mutual action plan we can share with procurement.

Traffic profile: ~120 req/min, bursts up to 450 for 5–10s, average payload ~1.2k tokens (embedding requests vary). We run behind a forward proxy and do key rotation every 30 days.

Could you share:
- SDK quickstart + code examples (token auth + rotation pattern)
- Recommended client-side retry/backoff for 429/503 and idempotency guidance
- A short checklist for endpoint migration (DNS vs config swap options)

I attached an initial requirements pdf with our constraints. Proposed timeline: staging integration this sprint (May 8–10), production cutover week of May 15. Is that realistic from your side?

Thanks,
Jared
---
Artera, Platform Engineering

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Artera → Redwood: kickoff + SDK + migration window

Jared — thanks, this is great context. Looping in Monica (CS lead) and Vivek (solutions/infra) to give detailed recommendations and own the mutual action plan.

Quick responses / plan:
- Timeline: staging May 8–10 looks fine; we’ll reserve a 2hr cutover window May 15 10:00–12:00 PT for production migration. Please confirm if that conflicts with your ops.
- Attachments: I’ve uploaded our integration matrix (attached) with suggested config keys and cutover checklist.
- Auth/key rotation: We recommend short-lived tokens (1 hour) with a rotating service account; token-exchange pattern below. Monica will coordinate a short SOW amendment for any private deployment requirements.

High-level SDK guidance (details to follow from Vivek):
- Client timeouts: request timeout = 10s for sync calls; read/stream timeout = 30s for streaming generation.
- Retries: linear backoff for 429 with jitter starting at 200ms, retry up to 6 times for idempotent calls, exponential backoff for 5xx.
- Idempotency: use client-generated request_id header for non-trivial side-effecting calls.
- Endpoint migration options: (A) DNS swap + TTL 60s during cutover, (B) config flag toggle if you’re using SDK and can update base_url atomically.

Next steps: Vivek will share concrete SDK snippets and a 1-page fallback flow (429/503/timeout) + attach the code bundle. Monica will send the mutual action plan and procurement checklist by EOD tomorrow.

–Steph
Steph Nguyen
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

2) For streaming reads: we sometimes see half-open connections when a client network is flaky. Is there a recommended client keepalive / reconnect pattern you advise?

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to run through the matrix.

—Jared
